classes.name: Elección de Presidenta o Presidente y Vicepresidenta o Vicepresidente del Estado
classes.name_en: President and vice president, elected on one ticket
classes.finest_note: Mesa de sufragio (polling table) inside each recinto, in the Atlas's votos_totales.csv and the official count's acta-level results
classes.note: Since 2009 a ticket wins with over 50% of valid votes, or 40% with a 10-point lead; otherwise a runoff between the top two within 60 days (CPE art. 166; Ley 026 arts. 52-53). Before 2009, when no ticket won an absolute majority, Congress chose among the top candidates (CPE 1967/2004 art. 90), so the popular vote is one contest and the congressional choice an indirect one (class presidente_congreso). The first popular runoff was held on 19 October 2025. The first presidential elections by restricted direct vote date from the 1840s; the first under universal suffrage was in 1956.

cadence.runoff_rule: Elected with over 50% of valid votes, or at least 40% with a 10-point lead over the runner-up; otherwise a runoff between the top two within 60 days; no runoff if a finalist withdraws 45 days before (Ley 026 art. 53).
cadence.locator: https://tcpbolivia.bo/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/CPE_2009.pdf (art. 166: "cincuenta por ciento más uno de los votos válidos; o que haya obtenido un mínimo del cuarenta por ciento de los votos válidos, con una diferencia de al menos diez por ciento"; art. 168: five years); the TSE sets each date by convocatoria

classes.name_en: Congressional choice of president when no ticket won an absolute majority
classes.note: Under CPE 1967 art. 90 (texts of 1994 and 2004), "Si en las elecciones generales ninguna de las fórmulas ... obtuviera la mayoría absoluta de sufragios válidos, el Congreso elegirá por mayoría absoluta" among the top three (top two from 1994). Congress chose the president after every general election from 1979 to 2002; in 2005 Evo Morales won an absolute majority. The votes of members of Congress are in the Congress's records, not OEP's.

classes.name: Elección de Diputadas y Diputados (uninominales, plurinominales y de circunscripciones especiales)
classes.finest_note: Mesa de sufragio (polling table) inside each recinto, in the Atlas's votos_totales.csv and the official count's acta-level results
classes.note: 130 deputies (CPE art. 146). Since 1997 a mixed-member compensatory system: single-member circunscripciones uninominales by plurality, and departmental list seats allocated by D'Hondt on the presidential vote among parties with 3% nationally, less the single-member seats won (Ley 026 art. 59). From 2009 seven circunscripciones especiales indígena originario campesinas elect one deputy each by plurality (art. 61). Split: 70 uninominal, 53 list, and 7 special in 2009 (Ley 026 art. 57); 63, 60, and 7 since Ley 421 of 2013, kept by Ley 1614 of 2025 after the 2024 census. Contests counted per election: each single-member and special district plus the nine departmental list contests. Before 1997 deputies were elected on departmental lists only (not counted here).

cadence.runoff_rule: A tie in a single-member or special district goes to a second vote within 28 days (Ley 026 arts. 60-61).

classes.name: Elección de Alcalde por el Concejo Municipal
classes.name_en: Mayors chosen by the council when no list won an absolute majority, 1985-2004
classes.note: "Si ninguno ... obtuviera la mayoría absoluta, el Concejo tomará a los dos que hubieran logrado el mayor número de sufragios ... y de entre ellos hará la elección por mayoría absoluta" (CPE 1967/2004 art. 200 VI), with a constructive censure vote after a year (art. 201). The councils' votes are municipal records that OEP does not publish.
classes.disposition_reason: Council votes are kept in each municipality's minutes; no national authority compiles them.

classes.name: Referendos municipales, regionales y de autonomía indígena originario campesina
classes.finest_note: Mesa de sufragio (polling table) inside each recinto, in the Atlas's votos_totales.csv and the official count's acta-level results
classes.note: Municipal referendums on exclusive municipal matters and cartas orgánicas, regional autonomy referendums, and votes to convert a municipality into an indigenous autonomy and approve its statute (Ley 026 arts. 13 and 24; Ley 031 arts. 50-54). Held: 6 December 2009 (Gran Chaco regional autonomy under Ley 4021 art. 76, and conversions of municipalities to indigenous autonomy under DS 231), 20 September 2015 (Charagua and Totora Marka statutes and cartas orgánicas), 20 November 2016 (15 entities, including the Gran Chaco statute, Uru Chipaya, Raqaypampa, and Gutiérrez), and 9 July 2017 (Huacaya and Macharetí).

classes.name: Conformación de gobiernos de las autonomías indígena originario campesinas
classes.note: Charagua Iyambae (from 2017), Uru Chipaya, Raqaypampa, Salinas, Kereimba Iyaambae (Gutiérrez), Jatun Ayllu Yura, the Territorio Indígena Multiétnico, and Huacaya choose their governments by normas y procedimientos propios under their statutes (CPE arts. 289-296; Ley 026 art. 74).
classes.disposition_reason: Authorities are chosen in community assemblies by each autonomy's own rules, not by ballot; OEP's SIFDE supervises and publishes reports and the names chosen, with no votes.

classes.name: Asambleas, cabildos y consulta previa
classes.note: Public meetings and the state's prior consultation of indigenous peoples on resource projects (Ley 026 arts. 35-41).
classes.disposition_reason: Not ballots: assemblies and cabildos decide in public meetings that OEP's SIFDE only observes and reports on (arts. 37-38), and prior consultation is a deliberative process.

classes.name: Organizaciones territoriales de base y juntas vecinales
classes.name_en: Neighborhood councils and grassroots territorial organizations
classes.note: Neighborhood and community organizations recognized under the 1994 popular participation law elect their own officers.
classes.disposition_reason: Civil-society organizations electing their own boards; no state election, register of results, or electoral authority.

classes.name: Elección interna de dirigencias y candidaturas de organizaciones políticas
classes.name_en: Party leadership and candidate selection other than the state-run primaries
classes.note: OEP supervises that parties choose leaders and candidates by their own internal rules (Ley 026 art. 49; Ley 1096).
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the parties under their own statutes; OEP only supervises and publishes no returns.
